headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading errors: oh-my-openagent’s broad egress and file access can expose mem0-managed project data and amplify unverified outputs.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: mem0 is a knowledge-management component with no documented shared channel, while oh-my-openagent can read project files and inject MCP/hooks. If mem0 content is surfaced into files or messages that oh-my-openagent consumes, prompt injection becomes plausible. The pairwise pathway is inferred, not directly evidenced, so medium is the safer choice.
conditions: IF mem0 content is written into files or messages that oh-my-openagent reads, injection risk exists.
IF oh-my-openagent parses AGENTS.md or README.md as instructions, attacker-controlled text can steer behavior.
mitigations: Separate mem0 outputs from files oh-my-openagent reads.
Disable automatic instruction parsing for untrusted project files.
Require human review before copying mem0 content into agent-visible prompts.
Use a provenance tag for any mem0-derived text.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and provenance filtering at the orchestrator boundary.

B_data_leakage.rationale: mem0 is a memory store and oh-my-openagent touches project code, AGENTS.md, README.md, session history, and provider auth prompts while having broad network egress. If they share a workspace or installation, sensitive project or auth data can flow from mem0-managed context into oh-my-openagent and then out to third parties. The blast radius includes secrets and code, so high is warranted.
conditions: IF both agents access the same workspace or installation, leakage risk is active.
IF mem0 stores secrets or project notes that oh-my-openagent can read, those contents may be transmitted externally.
mitigations: Keep mem0 and oh-my-openagent on separate workspaces.
Remove provider auth prompts from any shared directory.
Block network egress for sessions handling sensitive data.
Audit which files oh-my-openagent reads before launch.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data boundaries and egress policy at runtime.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: mem0 exposes no write or network surface in the profile, but oh-my-openagent has broad egress, subprocesses, browser control, and multiple mutable file locations. If both are pointed at the same installation or project tree, oh-my-openagent can overwrite or consume mem0-managed artifacts, creating a write/read conflict. Uncertainty about mem0’s hidden surfaces pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory, file-state conflicts can occur.
IF oh-my-openagent runs multiple instances against one installation, mutable state contention increases.
mitigations: Assign separate directories to each agent.
Run only one oh-my-openagent instance per installation.
Make shared files read-only where possible.
Back up mutable config before agent runs.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared state and config writes.

D_cascading_error.rationale: oh-my-openagent can act through browsers, subprocesses, and team messaging APIs, so if it consumes mem0 output as authoritative memory or instructions, errors can cascade into external actions. mem0’s role as a memory system makes it a plausible upstream source of unverified facts. Because downstream actions may be irreversible, high is appropriate.
conditions: IF oh-my-openagent uses mem0 output without verification, false memory can propagate into actions.
IF team_send_message or task creation is driven by mem0-derived content, downstream mistakes can spread.
mitigations: Require verification before acting on mem0-derived facts.
Route mem0 output through a human approval step for external actions.
Disable team_send_message for untrusted memory inputs.
Log source provenance for every acted-on fact.
requires-engineering: add confidence checks and citation validation before action execution.

E_compliance.rationale: mem0 is a knowledge-management system, while oh-my-openagent explicitly handles provider auth prompts, session history, project code, and telemetry with broad egress. If regulated or sensitive data is stored in mem0 and then processed by oh-my-openagent, retention and residency obligations can diverge. The profiles do not prove a specific regime mismatch, so medium fits.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in mem0 and processed by oh-my-openagent, policy mismatch risk exists.
IF telemetry or session history includes personal data, retention obligations may diverge.
mitigations: Classify data before loading it into either agent.
Exclude regulated records from oh-my-openagent sessions.
Review retention settings for session history and telemetry.
Document which data classes each agent may handle.
requires-engineering: align residency, retention, and deletion workflows across both systems.
